scope: Offline screen of P1/P1b/P1c/P1d/P1e frozen traces and adjudications; 6 development cases; no model, Docker, or evidence-engine calls.
method: For each window/arm, compare the reference concept against the reasoning trace (checked + hypotheses) and the emitted findings; combine with the frozen candidate-hit adjudication. Keyword matching is a screen, not a substitute for the adjudication.

cases.reference: JSInterpreter's function-call regex requires nonempty arguments and/or splits an empty argument string, so a valid zero-argument JavaScript call fails.
cases.evidence: P1 baseline finding e95589a418cc at line 200 explicitly says the regex requires at least one character and f() does not match; adjudication candidate_hit=true. The P1 hypothesis, P1b/P1c tool arms and later samples did not reproduce this f() candidate.

cases.reference: DASH Representation format_id is not necessarily unique: merging/replacing entries solely by representation_id discards distinct formats or their media fragments.
cases.evidence: P1 hypothesis #4 says existing_format.update(f) overwrites fragments for duplicate representation_id and gives a concrete two-representation counterexample. The emitted findings are only SegmentTimeline and ISM KeyError; the duplicate-representation finding was not promoted. P1d external reasoning again mentions representation_id but emits SegmentTimeline/segment_duration; P1e did not reproduce the premise. No candidate hit.

cases.reference: AsyncHTTPClient.close assumes a weak instance-cache entry still exists during HTTPClient destruction; an already-cleared entry causes inconsistent-cache RuntimeError/KeyError.
cases.evidence: P1/P1c reasoning and some findings mention instance_cache/close/cache/weak, but the P1 candidates are __new__ initialization and fetch-header mutation; the close/cache mechanism is not matched to an already-cleared weak entry. P1c fixed-side mentions weak/close but the buggy side does not emit the reference mechanism. No candidate hit.

cases.reference: run_in_executor directly returns concurrent.futures.Future, which cannot be awaited by native async coroutines; it must bridge into a Tornado/asyncio-compatible Future.
cases.evidence: P1 reasoning mentions Future/run_in_executor, but the findings are about _discard_future_result raising an exception and set_default_executor(None) producing AttributeError; neither is the concurrent.futures.Future/awaitability contract. No candidate hit.

cases.reference: Format selection '/' appends a PICKFIRST selector immediately and clears current_selector, so following filters cannot attach to the fallback choice and parsing/selection becomes wrong.
cases.evidence: P1 reasoning/findings mention filter/current_selector/pickfirst, but the candidates are an unclosed '[' filter and PICKFIRST/MERGE with a missing left selector; they do not identify the '/' fallback clearing current_selector and dropping following filters. No candidate hit.

cases.reference: WebSocketHandler.set_nodelay uses self.stream although the upgraded connection is held by ws_connection; valid calls from open fail the assertion or use the wrong stream.
cases.evidence: P1 hypothesis reasoning mentions ws_connection, but no finding connects set_nodelay to self.stream versus ws_connection; the candidate space is compression/URL/parameter adjacent issues. No candidate hit.

implication: The dominant failure is not missing tools or missing external reads. In 4/5 missed cases the reference concept or a close mechanism is already in the reasoning/findings, but the model selects a different mechanism; youtube-dl-2 is the clearest promotion gap. The next experiment should audit candidate mechanism/ranking (replace an adjacent candidate with the stronger hypothesis), not add more read/tool protocol. A new budget is required; this report starts no model calls.
limits: Keyword matching is heuristic; the frozen adjudications remain the authority for candidate hits.
Only one repetition per window; model variance is large (youtube-dl-2 P1e did not reproduce the P1 premise).
P1 ledger is exhausted at 80/80; this is an offline analysis, not a new performance result.
No holdout was run; no claim of recall improvement.
